Q1: Phosphorous acid exhibits known hazards for oral (ORL1) and dermal/eye (SKN1) exposure, based on internationally recognized GHS classifications. However, its hazard profiles for carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, reproductive toxicity (CMR4), environmental impact (ENV4), endocrine disruption (EDC4), inhalation (IHL4), and organ/systemic effects (OGN4) are currently data deficient (Tier 4).
Q2: While Phosphorous acid is not on any "lists of concern," it is included on the SCIL Yellow Triangle list. This designation indicates it meets Safer Choice Criteria as a best-in-class chemical for its function, but still carries some identified hazard profile issues that highlight the need for safer chemistry innovation.
Q3: Phosphorous acid is structurally well-defined as a "Small Molecule" with a clear molecular formula (H3O3P), and is not classified as a UVCB. With 1056 SciFinder references, its research volume is above the median for our limited dataset of fracking and petrochemical materials, yet a significant portion of its hazard profile (5 out of 7 classes) remains data deficient (Tier 4).
